{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=theoretical+frameworks+for+machine+agency+and+moral+responsibility+attribution&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7483422\", \"title\": [\"Self-Good Desire and the Moral Agency of Artificial Intelligence :A Criterion of Life Integrity for Responsibility Attribution\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The increasing autonomy of artificial intelligence has intensified the \\\"responsibility gap\\\" and the debate over AI moral agency. Existing accounts commonly appeal to rational capacity, sentience, or functional performance, but these criteria do not fully explain either the motivational basis for taking norms as reasons or the conditions under which a subject can bear ultimate moral responsibility. Drawing on the framework developed in On Self-Good Desire, this paper argues that \\\"self-good desire\\\" (sishan yuqiu) is a motivationally necessary condition of full moral agency. It denotes an intrinsic, selfnurturing motivational structure through which a living subject maintains its existence, improves its condition, and pursues its development, unfolding into eleven root desires: self-preservation, self-care, self-enrichment, self-beautification, self-joy, self-compassion, self-reflection, self-confidence, selfstrengthening, self-respect, and freedom. \\\"Life integrity\\\" here does not reduce moral agency to a particular biological substrate; rather, it refers to an integrated organization of self-maintenance, felt value, diachronic identity, and self-concern. Self-good desire is not sufficient for full moral agency, which also requires normative understanding, behavioral control, and responsibility-bearing capacity. On this account, current AI systems can represent norms and simulate forms of moral reasoning, yet there is presently insufficient warrant to attribute to them endogenous needs, first-person experience, enduring self-concern, or genuinely self-generated stakes. They therefore should not be treated as full moral agents. When AI systems cause harm, ultimate moral responsibility should ordinarily remain with human and institutional actors and be allocated by reference to control, causal contribution, benefit, foreseeability, and duties of care. The paper also addresses objections concerning infants, animals, corporations, functionalism, biologism, and future artificial agents, while remaining conditionally open to future artificial systems that might develop functionally equivalent forms of endogenous concern.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7483422\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1163/9789004697676_011\", \"title\": [\"Genetic Attribution, Moral Agency, and Moral Responsibility from the Perspective of African Philosophy\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1163/9789004697676_011\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024, 5, 18]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199266302.003.0006\", \"title\": [\"Moral Failures and Moral Responsibility: Recklessness, Weakness, Compulsion\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199266302.003.0006\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2003, 10, 2]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.5040/9781978721685.ch-2\", \"title\": [\"Agency, Moral Responsibility, and Addiction\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.5040/9781978721685.ch-2\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "71b42af93f9bc5daced13cd73a7d815357bdecf4e2804faac5b45bb0927d7aba", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "responsibility_formation", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.2139/ssrn.7483422", "doi:10.1163/9789004697676_011", "doi:10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199266302.003.0006", "doi:10.5040/9781978721685.ch-2"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7483422", "https://doi.org/10.1163/9789004697676_011", "https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199266302.003.0006", "https://doi.org/10.5040/9781978721685.ch-2"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
